PullRequest.Title: Remove obsolete production build infrastructure
PullRequest.Body:
Cleanup after #336093, #336120, and #336109 (all merged). This branch now includes `main`.

Related legacy-build discussions: #251233, #276144.

## Changes

- Remove obsolete production compile/mangle/bundle/minify chains, stale tasks/scripts, and exclusive helpers: **6 direct dependency declarations and 22 lockfile entries**.
- Retain active Gulp, TypeScript/TSB, Monaco, extension, localization, source-map, and SVG pipelines.
- Share bootstrap/target definitions, reject missing required bootstraps, and honor CDN source-map URLs for the additional Dev Tunnels browser bundle.

## Validation (local)

- **190 tests**, build-tool/source typechecks, hygiene, and ESLint passed.
- Audited 303 tasks and 48 packaging routes in local/CI modes; built all four minified targets and verified resources, NLS, metadata, and map publication.
- Windows server-web packaging/CLI help and Monaco distribution/XLF export passed. Worktree builds supplied CI commit metadata. Browser UI and translated Monaco packs were not tested.

## Deliberate boundaries

- TypeScript private/protected-name mangling is retired; native `#private` lowering remains.
- Preload map fixes stay separate in #336204; its shared-type contract is preserved here.
- Unicode output validation remains separate as agreed; #336098 concerns escaping, not that validation policy.

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop, server, server-web, and standalone-web production bundle/package tasks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each selected Gulp packaging task must finish extension preparation, spawn and await one build/next/index.ts bundle process, then copy/package filesystem outputs. These remain on the build critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn build/next/index.ts to run the esbuild production bundle for the selected target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One child process per selected target/minification task; internal entry-point esbuild builds remain concurrently scheduled as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same helper and subprocess path was already selected for all active packaging because useEsbuildTranspile was a constant true.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The subprocess must complete before packaging starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run extension-specific esbuild/type-check processes while collecting local extension package streams.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one configured build process plus type-check streams per selected local extension, merged across the effective local-extension set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed disableMangle argument was unused by fromLocal, so extension selection, process count, and merge concurrency are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All selected extension streams must finish before core bundling/package completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read source/resource/dependency trees and write bundled and packaged outputs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Scales with target entry points, curated resources, built-in extensions, and production dependencies; grouping and deduplication are unchanged by this cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Active esbuild packaging already performed these reads/writes; the diff removes dormant legacy alternatives and shares target metadata without adding scans or copies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bundle output and packaging writes must finish before artifacts are complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selected build targets, target entry-point count, curated resource count, built-in extension count, and production dependency files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Gulp keeps major stages in series. The bundle subprocess uses existing Promise.all entry-point concurrency; extension streams remain merged with their existing concurrency. The diff neither adds a limiter nor increases aggregate concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tasks produce fresh output directories and do not add a new cache. Cold and warm behavior are unchanged for the active esbuild path; no cache key, miss, or coalescing logic changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted useEsbuildTranspile definition is visibly constant true, and the prior packaging branch therefore already called runEsbuildBundle with the same target and sequencing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact target build duration and repository resource counts vary by platform, but the before/after path and boundary cardinalities are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR removes unreachable legacy production branches and preserves the active build's subprocess, filesystem, cardinality, and concurrency behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dev Tunnels browser SDK bundle emitted as part of web-capable production targets
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After core resources and standalone files, a web/server-web build awaits the additional SDK esbuild invocation and its JavaScript/source-map writes before SVG optimization and overall bundle completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Esbuild bundles the browser SDK dependency graph.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One esbuild build per web-capable target bundle invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK esbuild invocation already occurred once on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The SDK bundle must finish before the target bundle can complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return the JavaScript and linked source map in outputFiles, decode the JavaScript, rewrite its sourceMappingURL, and retain both outputs until manual writing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly two expected outputs for one outfile with a linked external map; allocation scales linearly with this single SDK bundle and map size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Esbuild previously wrote the JavaScript and map directly; Node did not receive outputFiles or decode/rewrite the JavaScript.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The in-memory transfer/rewrite and two sequential writes occur before bundle completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create output directories and write devTunnelsModule.js plus devTunnelsModule.js.map.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two output writes and at most two idempotent mkdir calls per invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Esbuild itself wrote the same two output files; the diff changes ownership rather than materially increasing write cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The bundled Dev Tunnels SDK dependency graph and resulting JavaScript/source-map byte size, not repository item count or user data.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One SDK build is awaited. Its two output writes are serial; there is no per-module or per-resource fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No explicit bundle cache exists before or after. Every invocation rebuilds the SDK; the diff does not create repeated misses or disable coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that write:false adds one bounded in-memory JS/map transfer and rewrite; high that output cardinality is only two and invocation cardinality is one per web-capable bundle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact generated byte size is not established from the diff, so the incremental IPC/allocation and text-copy cost cannot be shown to materially affect overall production build latency or peak memory.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Although the diff adds bounded serialization/allocation to support CDN map URLs, it is a single two-file bundle with no multiplicative fan-out or retention, and the evidence does not establish a material build regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local compile-client and watch-client development workflow
Scenarios.CriticalPath: compile-client cleans out, copies/generated metadata, then runs the stream compiler and writes output. watch-client runs the existing type-check and metadata/codicon watchers in parallel.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan source files and emit development JavaScript and generated metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Scales with the source tree for a full compile and changed files for watch operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: compile-client passed build=false, which selected the same non-build esbuild-transpile configuration now hard-coded after removing obsolete production options.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A full compile must emit all selected files; watch progress depends on changed-file processing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run tsgo/type-check watcher and related build watchers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One type-check watcher plus the existing metadata/codicon watchers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed no-op watch branch was unreachable because useEsbuildTranspile was constant true; active watcher count and work are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Watchers run continuously; initial readiness follows their existing initialization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Full source-file count for compile-client and changed-file frequency for watch-client.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The compile task remains a stream pipeline; watch-client retains its existing parallel watcher set. No changed scheduling increases file-operation or subprocess concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing compiler/watch incremental state is unchanged. The removed flag did not alter the active true branch, so cold initialization and warm incremental behavior remain the same.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the explicit old call argument build=false and the deleted constant useEsbuildTranspile=true.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Machine-dependent compile duration is irrelevant to causality because the effective options and active branches are equivalent before and after.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the signature cleanup preserves the active development compile/watch behavior.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold install, the package manager resolves and downloads declared dependency graphs before build tooling can run; warm installs can reuse the package-manager cache.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/download npm packages removed with obsolete bundling, SVG-minification, pump, and worker-pool infrastructure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six direct declarations and their transitive lock entries are removed; no replacement packages are added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff these obsolete packages remained in the install graph even though the active production path did not use them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold installation performs fewer registry/package downloads; warm installs avoid or reduce cache lookups/extraction for these packages.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract and store installed dependency files under node_modules/cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Reduced by the removed direct and transitive package graph.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed packages previously consumed installation I/O and disk space.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Installation must complete before build scripts run.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold dependency graph size and package archive/file count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Controlled by npm; the diff reduces work items and does not introduce a request burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold installs avoid downloads/extraction for removed packages; warm installs no longer need their cached artifacts in the resolved graph. No application cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from direct manifest and lockfile removals.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Registry latency and local cache state vary, but directionality is an improvement rather than a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding; dependency removal reduces installation network, filesystem, and disk costs.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 28 changed files and all diff pages. Traced production packaging, extension builds, Dev Tunnels source-map emission, local compile/watch, and dependency installation. The active esbuild path and its expensive boundary cardinalities were already in use; the only new bounded in-memory output rewrite affects one two-file SDK bundle and lacks evidence of material impact, so no actionable performance regression was submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
